title: Customers Without Orders
statement:
Find the customers who have never placed an order.

The `customers` table has one row per customer:

- `id`: the customer's id
- `name`: the customer's name (no two customers share one)
- `signed_up`: the date they created their account

The `orders` table has one row per order:

- `id`: the order's id
- `customer_id`: the `id` of the customer who placed it
- `amount`: what the order cost

Return one column, `name`, with the name of every customer who has no row in `orders`, sorted by `name`. If every customer has ordered, the result is empty.

Expected output:

```text
    name
-------------
 Carlos Vega
 Leo Martins
 Tom Becker
(3 rows)
```
setup:
CREATE TABLE customers (
  id integer PRIMARY KEY,
  name text NOT NULL,
  signed_up date NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE orders (
  id integer PRIMARY KEY,
  customer_id integer NOT NULL REFERENCES customers (id),
  amount numeric(8, 2) NOT NULL
);

INSERT INTO customers (id, name, signed_up) VALUES
  (1, 'Priya Shah', '2026-01-05'),
  (2, 'Tom Becker', '2026-01-12'),
  (3, 'Aisha Bello', '2026-02-01'),
  (4, 'Leo Martins', '2026-02-14'),
  (5, 'Hana Sato', '2026-03-03'),
  (6, 'Carlos Vega', '2026-03-20');

INSERT INTO orders (id, customer_id, amount) VALUES
  (501, 1, 34.00),
  (502, 3, 12.50),
  (503, 1, 80.00),
  (504, 5, 22.75),
  (505, 3, 9.99);

hints: A `LEFT JOIN` keeps every customer, even one with no matching order.
When a customer has no order, every column that comes from `orders` is NULL in that row. Test it with `IS NULL`.

sql.starter:
-- TODO: keep only the customers who have no orders
SELECT c.name
FROM customers AS c
ORDER BY c.name;
sql.solution:
SELECT c.name
FROM customers AS c
LEFT JOIN orders AS o ON o.customer_id = c.id
WHERE o.id IS NULL
ORDER BY c.name;
